title: Do somatotypes exist?
summary: NH argues somatotypes don't exist: the label crams too many unrelated traits into three categories and implies determinism. Skinny or fat is mostly a response to environment, and he cites his own path from spaghetti-armed 'ectomorph' and 240 lb 'endomorph' to a muscular physique. Anyone can build a muscular body with hard work.

claims.claim: An overarching concept is only useful if its subcategories are clearly defined; somatotypes lump limb length, bone density, metabolism, TDEE, response to volume and intensity, fat and muscle gain, hormones and insertions into one label, which makes it useless.
He plans a hierarchy of terms: somatotypes, then limb-dominant vs torso-dominant, then specific achievable body archetypes he named (spider, turtle, bear, etc.).

Ectomorphs are described as lanky and skinny, mesomorphs as hard and muscular, endomorphs as thick-boned and fat-prone; the system is really a value pyramid with the mesomorph on top, which is childish.

Apparently 80% of YouTube fitness is ectomorphs; that's called being skinny, not a body type determined at birth. Feed an 'endomorph' less and he becomes an 'ectomorph'; the body responds to environment.

No one is born muscular; teens with a favorable hormonal profile who stay active end up more muscular, but they still did something. Genetic freaks who grow doing nothing are exceptions, not a category.
He was lanky with spaghetti arms into his 20s despite hard training and eating, and people told him there was no point; now viewers ask if he is a mesomorph.
Hardgainer is just another name for ectomorph; a muscular body is achievable by everyone, your starting point only makes it harder.
During his bulk days he weighed 240 lb and was fat, then lost the weight.
A big bone structure (thick wrists, ankles, knees, wide shoulders) is a frame to pack muscle on; you don't have to be fat underneath.
Training advice by somatotype is baseless: you can't tell from someone's outside shape how they respond to volume, intensity or which lifts cause damage without injury.
To make somatotypes work you'd need 200 categories and even then it would fail because people change.
The environment you put yourself in matters more than the one you were born into; most inborn limits can be overcome with work, but if you accept that it won't get better, it won't.
